out.other_title: Doubly-efficient debate: poly-time honest prover, constant human-judgement queries
out.rationale: Brown-Cohen, Irving and Piliouras introduce doubly-efficient debate, in which two polynomial-time provers compete so that, under appropriate assumptions, any polynomial-time computation can be verified with a constant number of human-judgement queries. Brown-Cohen et al. Both ask whether debate can work with efficient debaters, in different settings.

text: The authors state that existing recursive debate protocols suffer from the obfuscated arguments problem, where a dishonest debater can use a computationally efficient strategy that forces an honest opponent to solve a computationally intractable problem to win. They propose a new recursive debate protocol that, under certain stability assumptions, ensures an honest debater can win with a strategy requiring computational efficiency comparable to its opponent.
title: Prover-estimator debate mitigates the obfuscated arguments problem in recursive debate
